scope: Theorem 3.4 (Expansion, obstacle detours, and delivery) of the manuscript “Incompressible Box Transport and Finite Computation” (preprints/Incompressible-Box-Transport-and-Finite-Computation-October-6-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2505dc09d3f2c24b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 10-11. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let Qi = ai + Q3 j=1[−hij, hij] and Q′ i = bi + Q3 j=1[−kij, kij] be rational solid boxes, with positive half-widths, each family pairwise 10 disjoint. Suppose sij = kij/hij and Q j sij = 1. An effective compactly supported smooth solenoidal field, zero outside the time interval [1/4, 3/4], has time-one map ai + y 7−→ bi + diag(si1, si2, si3)y on a neighborhood of each Qi.
